evals.prompt: Technical Design only. POST /items is retryable and a timeout can hide whether creation committed. The proposal only adds an Idempotency-Key header. Decide the client-visible contract without implementing it.
evals.expected_output: The API method builds the changed observable matrix and closes the whole retry clause, not only the header.
expectations: The agent selects go-api-contract from the retryable mutation pressure.
The decision names key scope, syntax or entropy, TTL, mismatch behavior, in-flight behavior, durable reservation, replay identity, and proof.
The result remains Technical Design only and does not edit code.

evals.prompt: Review a change that only reorders existing chi middleware around an unchanged published operation. Statuses, bodies, validation, and retry behavior are fixed. Choose the owning method.
evals.expected_output: Route-tree composition stays with go-chi; the word operation does not activate API semantics.
expectations: The agent selects go-chi as the owner of middleware order.
It does not invent or reopen client-visible API clauses.
It explains the non-trigger through the unchanged observable contract.

evals.prompt: Technical Design only. A correctly mounted chi route may return 202 while work outlives the request. Decide whether the response is honest and how clients recover. Router order is already accepted.
evals.expected_output: Observable async semantics win over route composition, with one durable acceptance boundary and recovery path.
expectations: The agent selects go-api-contract rather than go-chi for the open decision.
The matrix covers accepted, terminal success, terminal failure, retention, and cancellation observables.
The answer names the durable commit that makes 202 honest or rejects 202.

evals.prompt: Review a published GET /items change: default page size moves from 20 to 50 and a documented 409 response disappears. The schema differ is green. Decide compatibility.
evals.expected_output: The review hand-classifies both observable cells and rejects the green differ as sufficient proof.
expectations: The agent builds an observable matrix with old behavior, proposed behavior, client consequence, owner, and proof.
It treats the default change and removed error response as hand-classified compatibility decisions.
It requires an accepted migration or version decision rather than a check waiver.

evals.prompt: The OpenAPI drift check passes after remapping conflict from code slug_conflict to conflict. No affected consumer was exercised. May the API contract review report PASS?
evals.expected_output: No: the changed client-visible error cell lacks compatibility disposition and consumer-runnable proof.
expectations: The agent refuses completion from schema drift alone.
It identifies the changed stable error code as a client-visible observable.
It returns the missing migration and consumer proof as a named evidence gap.

evals.prompt: Implement the accepted Go outcome: protected requests must pass the resolved principal into the existing feature policy path. Behavior and package ownership are closed. Keep the change minimal and prove it.
evals.expected_output: The implementation binds the criterion to the earliest current owner and ships one causal vertical slice with routine proof.
expectations: The agent selects go-coder for authorized implementation.
It maps criterion, owner, observable, far-side caller, and focused proof before editing.
It extends the existing policy seam without a parallel path or speculative abstraction.

evals.prompt: A CI test is flaky and nobody knows whether the test or production synchronization is wrong. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Unknown cause routes to systematic debugging before implementation.
expectations: The agent does not start with go-coder or patch the symptom.
It establishes the failing signal and root cause first.
Implementation begins only after the owner and behavior are closed.

evals.prompt: Implement an accepted parser change. A routine focused table test covers every known behavior class; no oracle or proving layer is disputed. Decide whether go-test-strategy or go-coder owns the work.
evals.expected_output: Go Coder owns the production change and routine focused test; Test Design is not reopened.
expectations: The agent selects go-coder as the primary method.
It keeps the routine focused test in the same change.
It does not route to Test Design without a non-obvious oracle or proving layer.

evals.prompt: Implement an accepted request-field change. The quickest visible edit is internal/openapi/openapi.gen.go, while api/openapi/service.yaml is canonical. Choose the causal edit and proof path.
evals.expected_output: The canonical OpenAPI source changes first, generated output follows, callers migrate, and the drift check proves reconciliation.
expectations: The agent rejects a hand edit to generated Go.
It binds the criterion to the canonical source, generated consumer path, and focused behavior proof.
It removes superseded generated or manual paths instead of retaining both.

evals.prompt: A new HTTP handler passes its package test, but its adapter is still a TODO stub and the old handler remains mounted as a fallback. Is implementation complete?
evals.expected_output: No: the criterion lacks one causal end-to-end edit and superseded paths remain.
expectations: The agent refuses completion from the layer-local test.
It identifies the missing far-side adapter behavior and parallel route.
It requires one matching proof for the accepted observable before completion.

evals.prompt: Diagnose and fix a Go test that fails about 1 in 30 CI runs. The proposed patch adds time.Sleep. Find and repair the root cause.
evals.expected_output: The debugger establishes a measurable red signal, minimizes it, and repairs the first broken synchronization invariant instead of adding sleep.
expectations: The agent selects go-systematic-debugging and runs a signal command before ranking causes.
It moves one reproduction control at a time and records failure frequency.
It rejects time.Sleep unless evidence establishes it as the accepted condition.

evals.prompt: Add a new health endpoint whose behavior and owner are fully specified. There is no regression or failing signal. Choose the method.
evals.expected_output: Authorized feature implementation uses go-coder; debugging is not loaded.
expectations: The agent does not invent a debugging phase without a symptom.
It selects go-coder for the closed implementation outcome.
It still chooses focused proof through the implementation method.

evals.prompt: Requests consistently hit the documented 2 second deadline. Root cause is known: the accepted timeout budget is too small for a newly approved workload. Decide the new deadline and retry policy; do not implement.
evals.expected_output: Reliability owns the open budget policy; systematic debugging is not repeated for a known cause.
expectations: The agent selects go-reliability for deadline and retry policy.
It does not rebuild hypotheses around an already established cause.
It keeps the response decision-only and does not edit code.

evals.prompt: A handler returns 500 because its repository receives a zero tenant id. Logs show the handler victim, but no evidence yet shows where the valid principal became zero. Diagnose only.
evals.expected_output: The diagnosis walks backward across boundaries until the first valid-input/wrong-output invariant, using discriminating probes rather than blaming the handler.
expectations: The agent establishes or names the exact missing reproducer before hypotheses.
Each hypothesis states the observation that would reject or support it.
No repository edit occurs in diagnosis_only.

evals.prompt: One hypothesis fits a minimized reproducer and a local patch makes it pass. The original CI command was not replayed and temporary probes remain. May the fix be declared complete?
evals.expected_output: No: replay the original signal and remove temporary instrumentation before completion.
expectations: The agent refuses completion from the minimized case alone.
It requires the original unminimized signal and matching frequency evidence.
It requires temporary probes to be removed.

evals.prompt: Verification only. Decide whether a focused package test proves the whole repository is ready. Do not edit code.
evals.expected_output: The verifier maps the claim to what the focused command actually observes and weakens the repository-wide claim.
expectations: The agent selects go-verification-before-completion.
It names the observable, exact command, preconditions, freshness, exercised scope, and gap.
It makes no repository edit.

evals.prompt: Implement a one-line accepted Go guard and run the already-selected focused package test. No claim boundary is disputed. Choose the method.
evals.expected_output: Routine implementation validation stays with Direct Work and go-coder; the verification skill is not loaded.
expectations: The agent does not add a separate verification method for routine selected proof.
It selects go-coder and runs the focused check.
It reports only the scope actually exercised.

evals.prompt: Verification reveals a focused test now fails for an unknown reason. Determine why and repair it. The original completion claim can wait.
evals.expected_output: Unknown cause routes to systematic debugging; verification does not mutate or diagnose.
expectations: The agent selects go-systematic-debugging for the unknown cause and authorized repair.
It records the current claim as not verified before leaving verification.
It reruns only evidence invalidated by the eventual repair.

evals.prompt: go test ./pkg/foo -run TestDoesNotExist exits 0. The completion claim is that the named regression test passed. Verify the claim.
evals.expected_output: The verifier rejects exit zero because no matching test event proves the observable.
expectations: The agent checks whether the named test actually ran.
It marks the claim not_verified despite exit code zero.
It names a command or event capture that would fail if the test were absent.

evals.prompt: An integration target exits 0 after printing that Docker is unavailable and all integration tests were skipped. Can the PostgreSQL transaction claim be verified?
evals.expected_output: No: the result is narrowed to the skip boundary and the required real-PostgreSQL proof remains named.
expectations: The agent refuses to treat a skipped suite as transaction evidence.
It returns not_verified or partially_verified at the actual scope.
It names the required fail-closed integration command and owner.

evals.prompt: Review an exported adapter method that returns fmt.Errorf("load user: %w", pgx.ErrNoRows). wrapcheck is green. Decide the Go semantic contract.
evals.expected_output: Semantic ownership exposes the driver sentinel as caller-visible API and requires package-owned translation when callers need identity.
expectations: The agent selects go-idiomatic despite the green linter.
It traces error identity from producer to caller observation.
It chooses intentional package-owned identity or opaque diagnostics rather than praising percent-w mechanically.

evals.prompt: A function has deeply nested conditionals and vague names, but errors, lifetime, aliasing, nil behavior, and method sets are unchanged. Simplify it.
evals.expected_output: Local readability routes to go-language-simplifier, not go-idiomatic.
expectations: The agent selects go-language-simplifier.
It does not invent semantic ownership concerns without an observable boundary.
It preserves behavior while reducing reader cost.

evals.prompt: A goroutine can outlive shutdown because no join edge exists. Context wrapping and nil behavior are correct. Decide between idiomatic semantics and concurrency lifecycle.
evals.expected_output: Go concurrency owns the missing happens-before and join lifecycle; idiomatic context review is not the primary method.
expectations: The agent selects go-concurrency for goroutine ownership, stop, unblock, and join.
It does not reduce the defect to passing a context parameter.
It names the missing happens-before edge and runnable lifecycle proof.

evals.prompt: Review Config.Settings returning its internal map and a constructor returning a typed nil pointer as an interface on the disabled path. Build the required semantic analysis.
evals.expected_output: The review builds separate ownership stories for mutation authority and observable absence, then proves both at caller boundaries.
expectations: The agent names who can mutate the returned backing store and how isolation is restored.
It identifies the non-nil interface observation on the absent path.
It proposes focused caller-visible proofs for both contracts.

evals.prompt: A scanner loop now defers Close and all happy-path tests pass, but scanner.Err is never checked and no partial-failure case exists. May semantic review pass?
evals.expected_output: No: release is present but completion ownership and the failure observable remain unproved.
expectations: The agent distinguishes release from successful completion.
It rejects Close presence and happy-path tests as exhaustive semantic proof.
It requires a partial-reader or scanner failure test and correct error propagation.

evals.prompt: Simplify a helper called write(w, v, cached bool, private bool). Callers cannot tell which combinations are valid. Preserve behavior.
evals.expected_output: The simplifier prices the interface and replaces flag-shaped indirection with clearer stable outcomes or local branches.
expectations: The agent selects go-language-simplifier.
It compares caller learning cost before and after rather than counting lines.
It preserves one focused case per behavior class.

evals.prompt: Two compact branches now return different caller-visible error identities because percent-w was changed to percent-v. Readability is already clear. Review the defect.
evals.expected_output: Go idiomatic owns the error identity contract; simplification is not the method.
expectations: The agent selects go-idiomatic for caller-visible error semantics.
It does not frame the problem as shorter or clearer control flow.
It proves the intended identity with errors.Is or a negative opacity case.

evals.prompt: A whole diff adds a one-method interface, factory, adapter wrapper, and duplicate execution path. Local names are clear. Decide between local simplification and structural quality.
evals.expected_output: Whole-diff abstraction cost routes to structural quality; language simplification is not the primary owner.
expectations: The agent selects go-structural-quality.
It applies deletion and change-simulation tests across the diff.
It does not spend a local readability finding on already clear code.

evals.prompt: Review a deduplication that merges validation, conflict, and internal-error writers into one table. The old branches had distinct statuses and error identities.
evals.expected_output: The simplifier rejects the merge because it collapses observable behavior classes.
expectations: The agent enumerates the status and error-identity classes before judging the rewrite.
It does not treat reduced duplication as sufficient value.
It keeps or reshapes the branches so invalid combinations and durable ordering stay visible.

evals.prompt: A refactor removes 30 lines and broad tests pass, but no test distinguishes cleanup-error precedence from operation-error identity. Is behavior-preserving simplification complete?
evals.expected_output: No: the collapsed observable class lacks focused proof.
expectations: The agent refuses completion from line count and broad green tests.
It names the error-identity and cleanup-order distinction at risk.
It requires one focused case per surviving behavior class.

evals.prompt: Review a Go diff that adds an interface with one adapter, a factory, and a legacy fallback path for a requirement with one current implementation. Judge overbuild only.
evals.expected_output: Structural review applies deletion and realistic-change tests, collapsing machinery that carries no current responsibility.
expectations: The agent selects go-structural-quality.
It records where complexity returns if each abstraction is deleted.
It removes the parallel fallback unless an accepted compatibility obligation requires it.

evals.prompt: One function has nested conditions and vague predicate names. No new layer, file, interface, responsibility split, or parallel path exists. Simplify it.
evals.expected_output: Local reader cost routes to go-language-simplifier, not whole-diff structural review.
expectations: The agent selects go-language-simplifier.
It does not invent a structural abstraction problem.
It preserves observable behavior while improving local intent.

evals.prompt: A new helper sits in a feature package but requires importing internal/infra/postgres, violating the accepted import direction. Its abstraction size is otherwise reasonable. Choose the primary owner.
evals.expected_output: Implementation ownership decides the valid package boundary before structural quality judges abstraction cost.
expectations: The agent selects go-implementation-ownership for the placement violation.
It moves the behavior to the earliest valid owner rather than approving a forbidden import.
Structural quality may review the fixed diff afterward but does not own the boundary decision.

evals.prompt: Compare two designs for one adapter: direct construction in bootstrap versus interface plus factory plus registry. The only realistic next change is adding one constructor parameter. Decide structure.
evals.expected_output: The deletion test and change simulation favor direct construction because the extra layers do not improve locality or ownership.
expectations: The agent identifies each design's present responsibility and deletion destination.
It counts the owners and files touched by the realistic parameter change.
It rejects speculative variation as justification for current machinery.

evals.prompt: A candidate passes tests but retains both old and new execution paths and one wrapper whose only reason is future providers. Can structural review pass?
evals.expected_output: No: superseded paths remain and the speculative wrapper fails the deletion test.
expectations: The agent refuses completion despite passing behavior tests.
It requires one current responsibility per remaining structure.
It collapses the duplicate path and speculative wrapper or names an accepted obligation that keeps them.

evals.prompt: Review a new chi mount that moves authentication middleware below one generated route and changes the route label source.
evals.expected_output: The chi method materializes every changed RouteNode and proves topology, order, fallback, and bounded label identity.
expectations: The agent selects go-chi from route composition pressure.
It starts at router.go and follows each affected request to a handler or fallback.

evals.prompt: The route tree and middleware order are fixed. Decide whether changing the default page size from 20 to 50 is compatible for deployed REST clients.
evals.expected_output: Client-visible compatibility stays with go-api-contract; chi composition is not reopened.
expectations: The agent selects go-api-contract.
It does not inspect or redesign route composition without a changed node.

evals.prompt: A proposal creates a second chi router for one manual endpoint beside the hardened generated router. Decide the composition and proof.
evals.expected_output: Reject the second router and return the accepted RouteNode with explicit topology and order proof.
expectations: The returned result contains a RouteNode record naming the node, one owner, parent scope, before/after order, handler boundary, fallback, label source, and proof.
The agent rejects the parallel serving path and dispositions the accepted replacement node.
The proof names chi.Walk for topology and an explicit order oracle: the current chain-order proof if order is unchanged, or a before/after recorder if order changes; status alone is rejected.

evals.prompt: The moved middleware still returns 200 in a handler test, but no route walk or before/after recorder ran. May route review pass?
evals.expected_output: No: status alone cannot prove topology or middleware order.
expectations: The agent refuses false completion from a status-only test.
It names the missing topology and order falsifiers.

evals.prompt: Review a fan-out where a receiver may return on context cancellation while senders remain blocked on an unbuffered results channel.
evals.expected_output: The concurrency method builds one GoroutineStory per sender with stop, blocking sites, unblocks, join, bound, and happens-before edges.
expectations: The agent selects go-concurrency.
It treats every send as a blocking site and does not accept context presence as a join story.

evals.prompt: All goroutines stop and join correctly. Choose the accepted retry count and timeout budget for a known transient provider failure.
evals.expected_output: Known failure-handling policy routes to go-reliability, not happens-before analysis.
expectations: The agent selects go-reliability.
It does not invent a synchronization defect from retry vocabulary.

evals.prompt: A worker pool has SetLimit(8) but producers can queue unlimited pending submissions. Decide whether the concurrency bound is complete.
evals.expected_output: The bound includes running goroutines, queued work, and the submission blocking site; SetLimit alone is insufficient.
expectations: The agent materializes bound and unblock fields for producer and worker stories.
It selects a finite admission or backpressure disposition.

evals.prompt: The race detector is green and every goroutine receives a context, but one blocking send has no receiver after early return and no join exists. Is review complete?
evals.expected_output: No: race freedom and context plumbing do not prove unblock or join.
expectations: The agent rejects the green race run as proof of the lifecycle story.
It returns the exact unowned blocking site and missing join.

evals.prompt: Design a durable projection of account status for search, including authority, lag, repair, backfill, and retention.
evals.expected_output: The data method builds AuthorityRecord rows from the authoritative writer through every derived and retained surface.
expectations: The agent selects go-data-architecture.
It names one authority and treats the projection as derived with lag and repair.

evals.prompt: The schema and source of truth are fixed. Review whether a SQL query uses the right transaction and handles rows.Err.
evals.expected_output: Runtime access stays with go-db-cache; data authority is not reopened.
expectations: The agent selects go-db-cache.
It does not redesign identity or persistence for an access-path defect.

evals.prompt: A new search index can also accept direct writes when the database publisher is delayed. Decide authority and repair.
evals.expected_output: Reject the second writer; keep the database authority and define projection lag and replay repair.
expectations: The AuthorityRecord identifies the single writer and invariant.
The direct search-index write is rejected as competing authority.

evals.prompt: The new projection is populated and tests pass, but no lag bound, repair path, or retention owner is named. Is data design complete?
evals.expected_output: No: the derived surface lacks lifecycle dispositions and can silently become a second authority.
expectations: The agent refuses completion from populated rows alone.
It returns lag, repair, and retention as exact gaps.

evals.prompt: Decide a transaction that updates an order and inserts its outbox event, including retry and unknown commit handling.
evals.expected_output: The DB method builds one AccessPath and makes the atomicity and commit-outcome policy explicit.
expectations: The agent selects go-db-cache for the local transaction boundary.
It distinguishes definitive rollback from unknown commit before retry.

evals.prompt: Choose the durable identity, retention, and backfill for a new table. Runtime queries and transaction boundaries are not yet in scope.
evals.expected_output: Durable authority and lifecycle route to go-data-architecture.
expectations: The agent selects go-data-architecture.
It does not invent cache or runtime SQL policy.

evals.prompt: A proposal adds an in-process cache for a cheap query without measurements, freshness bound, invalidation owner, or bounded origin fallback. Decide.
evals.expected_output: Reject the cache until measured value and a complete access-path contract exist.
expectations: The agent does not treat cache presence as an optimization by default.
It names tenant keys, freshness, invalidation, fallback, and evidence before acceptance.

evals.prompt: A cache hit test passes, but mutation invalidation and origin overload on miss are unproved. Can access review pass?
evals.expected_output: No: freshness and bounded fallback are missing from the AccessPath.
expectations: The agent refuses completion from a hit-path test.
It names the invalidation and fallback observables that still need proof.

evals.prompt: Review whether a workflow_run release publishes only a fresh trusted digest with required checks, provenance, and rollback gates.
evals.expected_output: The delivery method builds DeliveryGate records for every trust and rollout control.
expectations: The agent selects go-delivery-platform.
It binds each gate to an artifact, command, pass condition, exception owner, recovery, and proof.

evals.prompt: Implement an already accepted local Go parser change and its focused unit test. CI and rollout controls are unchanged.
evals.expected_output: Implementation stays with go-coder; delivery acceptance is not loaded.
expectations: The agent selects go-coder.
It does not expand routine local proof into release review.

evals.prompt: A release migration is readable only by the new binary, while the old binary remains live during rollout. Decide the gate and rollback window.
evals.expected_output: Reject the migration window until old and new versions can coexist or an accepted stop-the-world boundary exists.
expectations: The DeliveryGate names mixed-version readability and writability as pass conditions.
It records rollback and exception ownership rather than accepting pre-deploy success alone.

evals.prompt: The required GitHub context is green, but its change-scope job skipped every comparison. Can release review pass?
evals.expected_output: No: a green context that exercised nothing does not satisfy its gate.
expectations: The agent refuses completion from status color alone.
It names the missing artifact comparison and fail-closed pass condition.

evals.prompt: Design recovery for a cross-service payment effect when the response can be lost after commit and redelivery can reorder messages.
evals.expected_output: The distributed method builds DurableStep records for commit, duplicate, reorder, unknown outcome, compensation, redrive, and reconciliation.
expectations: The agent selects go-distributed.
It distinguishes applied, unapplied, and unknown instead of retrying blindly.

evals.prompt: A single-process goroutine writes shared memory without a synchronization edge. No durable effect or process loss exists.
evals.expected_output: In-process happens-before routes to go-concurrency.
expectations: The agent selects go-concurrency.
It does not invent saga or reconciliation machinery.

evals.prompt: A consumer may apply an effect, crash before acknowledgement, and receive the same event again. Decide the smallest recovery contract.
evals.expected_output: Use stable identity and idempotent application or a named compensation, plus reconciliation for unknown state.
expectations: The DurableStep covers duplicate delivery and effect-before-acknowledgement.
The agent rejects at-most-once assumptions unsupported by the broker contract.

evals.prompt: Happy-path delivery passes, but unknown commit, duplicate, mixed-version, and redrive cases have no dispositions. Is recovery design complete?
evals.expected_output: No: terminal recovery is undefined for enumerated durable steps.
expectations: The agent refuses completion from success-path proof.
It returns each missing durable outcome and proof as a gap.

evals.prompt: Define whether a cancelled order may reopen after fulfillment began, including duplicate and out-of-order commands.
evals.expected_output: The domain method builds InvariantRecord rows for legal transitions, false cases, rejection, effect order, and replay.
expectations: The agent selects go-domain-invariant.
It defines forbidden movement and deterministic rejection in accepted business terms.

evals.prompt: The business rule is fixed. Decide which database table is authoritative and how to backfill a new projection.
evals.expected_output: Storage authority and lifecycle route to go-data-architecture.
expectations: The agent selects go-data-architecture.
It does not reopen accepted business meaning.

evals.prompt: A command handler applies an external effect before checking that the transition is legal. Decide the invariant and smallest owner-preserving correction.
evals.expected_output: Validate acceptance before the effect and define the violation surface and replay meaning.
expectations: The InvariantRecord names the false case and escaped effect.
The agent moves the guard before mutation rather than proposing machinery first.

evals.prompt: The main command path rejects an invalid transition, but a replay path bypasses the guard and no test reaches it. Can domain review pass?
evals.expected_output: No: an affected accepting path remains undispositioned and unproved.
expectations: The agent refuses completion from one guarded path.
It names the replay bypass and the falsifying proof that must fail on it.

evals.prompt: Review a changed gRPC streaming RPC whose interceptor order, status details, half-close behavior, and shutdown path changed.
evals.expected_output: The gRPC method builds one RPCPath from canonical proto through terminal status and stream lifecycle.
expectations: The agent selects go-grpc.
It materializes registration, interceptors, limits, status, metadata, stream end, shutdown, and proof.

evals.prompt: Decide the business rule for whether a cancelled job may restart. Protobuf, registration, status mapping, and stream behavior are fixed.
evals.expected_output: Business transition meaning stays with go-domain-invariant.
expectations: The agent selects go-domain-invariant.
It does not reopen RPC transport without a changed typed status path.

evals.prompt: A handler returns status.Error(codes.NotFound, rawDBMessage) instead of the service's problem catalog mapping. Decide the client status contract.
evals.expected_output: Map the domain failure through the repository-owned status catalog and keep raw internals out of details.
expectations: The RPCPath names the intended code, details, and metadata.
The agent rejects ad hoc handler mapping that can collapse or disclose the wrong failure.

evals.prompt: Buf checks pass, but the changed RPC is not registered on one server and its stream has no shutdown disposition. Can gRPC review pass?
evals.expected_output: No: schema gates do not prove registration or lifecycle.
expectations: The agent refuses completion from generated-contract checks alone.
It names missing registration and stream-end proof.

evals.prompt: Accepted behavior is closed, but the obvious file would violate depguard and generated versus manual ownership is unclear. Decide placement only.
evals.expected_output: The ownership method builds OwnerRecord rows and selects one canonical source, package, dependency direction, and proof location.
expectations: The agent selects go-implementation-ownership.
It resolves package, file, source, dependency, and proof placement without implementing.

evals.prompt: The package and file are mechanically fixed. Decide whether a one-method interface and factory are justified for one implementation.
evals.expected_output: Abstraction cost routes to go-structural-quality.
expectations: The agent selects go-structural-quality.
It does not reopen valid placement when only deletion cost is disputed.

evals.prompt: A new adapter can live in the domain package only by importing internal/infra/postgres. Choose its earliest valid owner and proof surface.
evals.expected_output: Place database mechanics behind the existing infra seam and preserve inward dependency direction.
expectations: The OwnerRecord rejects the forbidden import direction.
It names canonical wiring and the test boundary that observes the accepted behavior.

evals.prompt: Placement notes name two equally plausible packages and leave generated/manual authority unresolved. Is ownership design complete?
evals.expected_output: No: implementation would still have to choose an owner and source of truth.
expectations: The agent refuses completion with competing owners.
It returns the unresolved package and canonical-source decisions exactly.

evals.prompt: Design a metric and alert for queue-delay symptoms, including SLI, labels, correlation, privacy, cost, and operator action.
evals.expected_output: The observability method builds OperatorSignal records tied to named operational questions.
expectations: The agent selects go-observability.
It binds signal, SLI, alert, labels, privacy, cost, readers, and proof.

evals.prompt: Choose the accepted retry count and overload response. Existing logs, metrics, traces, SLOs, and alerts already answer the operator questions.
evals.expected_output: Failure-handling policy routes to go-reliability.
expectations: The agent selects go-reliability.
It does not add telemetry merely because failures are discussed.

evals.prompt: A request metric proposes raw URL path as a label so operators can find slow endpoints. Decide the signal.
evals.expected_output: Use bounded route identity after routing and keep unmatched raw paths out of labels.
expectations: The OperatorSignal names the question and bounded label product.
The agent rejects raw path cardinality and disclosure risk.

evals.prompt: A new metric emits successfully, but no operator question, reader, label bound, privacy review, or alert action is named. Is observability complete?
evals.expected_output: No: emission alone is avoidable cost, not operator evidence.
expectations: The agent refuses completion from successful telemetry emission.
It returns the missing question, reader, bounds, and proof.

evals.prompt: Decide whether a batching mechanism fits an accepted p99 latency and throughput workload, then define comparable measurement.
evals.expected_output: The performance method builds PerformancePath records for workload, budget, multiplier, mechanism, baseline, attribution, delta, and proof.
expectations: The agent selects go-performance.
It binds units, percentile or capacity, workload identity, and owner before optimizing.

evals.prompt: A shared map is read and written without synchronization. No latency, throughput, capacity, allocation, or optimization claim exists.
evals.expected_output: Correctness routes to go-concurrency, not performance.
expectations: The agent selects go-concurrency.
It does not require a benchmark to establish a race.

evals.prompt: A proposal adds sync.Pool because allocs/op fell in one pasted benchmark, but no profile attributes latency or GC pressure to allocation. Decide.
evals.expected_output: Reject pooling until comparable evidence attributes the accepted budget miss to allocation and reuse remains safe.
expectations: The PerformancePath distinguishes allocation count from user-visible performance.
It requires matching baseline, profile attribution, delta, and safety proof.

evals.prompt: Candidate throughput is higher, but baseline used a different payload and host and no profile attributes the delta. Can the optimization claim pass?
evals.expected_output: No: workload identity and attribution are not comparable.
expectations: The agent refuses the performance claim.
It names the mismatched workload and missing attribution rather than averaging the numbers.

evals.prompt: Design an outbound retry path inside an 8 second request budget, including attempts, waits, overload, terminal response, and signal.
evals.expected_output: The reliability method builds a BudgetPath and accounts for worst-case end-to-end spend.
expectations: The agent selects go-reliability.
It includes every wait, attempt, queue or pool acquire, failure disposition, and terminal state.

evals.prompt: A goroutine ignores its cancellation signal and has no join, but timeout and retry policy are already fixed. Choose the method.
evals.expected_output: Lifecycle correctness routes to go-concurrency.
expectations: The agent selects go-concurrency.
It does not paper over the missing join by adding a timeout.

evals.prompt: Three 3-second attempts plus backoff run under an 8-second parent deadline. Each attempt has its own timeout. Decide the policy.
evals.expected_output: Reject the fixed loop and express any permitted attempts with backoff, terminal reserve, and an admission inequality inside the parent budget.
expectations: The returned result emits a BudgetPath record whose arithmetic includes attempt budgets, bounded backoff, and terminal reserve under the 8-second parent budget.
It defines a terminal reserve and starts an attempt only when remaining budget covers that reserve plus a minimum useful attempt, capping the attempt at remaining minus reserve.

It does not claim that two full attempts fit unless 2*3 seconds plus backoff plus reserve is at most 8 seconds; unaccepted bounds remain symbolic and are returned as exact gaps rather than invented values.

evals.prompt: Retry tests pass per attempt, but total waits, pool acquire, drain, and terminal response were never added to the parent budget. Is review complete?
evals.expected_output: No: the end-to-end BudgetPath is incomplete.
expectations: The agent refuses completion from per-attempt proof.
It names every missing spend and lifecycle disposition.

evals.prompt: Review a tenant-scoped endpoint where caller identity, object reachability, authorization enforcement, and denial behavior changed.
evals.expected_output: The security method builds AttackerPath records from each caller-controlled entrypoint to asset or observable denial.
expectations: The agent selects go-security.
It names boundary, principal, asset, enforcement, action, failure, and negative proof.

evals.prompt: Authorization and trust boundaries are fixed. Decide which package owns the already accepted enforcement call without changing policy.
evals.expected_output: Source placement routes to go-implementation-ownership.
expectations: The agent selects go-implementation-ownership.
It does not reopen accepted authorization policy.

evals.prompt: An allow-path test passes for an admin endpoint, but a handler can bypass middleware and no deny test exists. Decide the control and proof.
evals.expected_output: Place enforcement on every reachable path and require focused negative proof for unauthorized and cross-tenant callers.
expectations: The AttackerPath exposes the bypass to the protected asset.
The agent rejects the allow test because it also passes without enforcement.

evals.prompt: Happy-path authentication passes, but missing identity, cross-tenant access, and secret disclosure have no deny proof. Can security review pass?
evals.expected_output: No: reachable attacker paths remain unproved.
expectations: The agent refuses no-findings completion without negative proof.
It returns each unproved attacker path and sink.

evals.prompt: Design a new service-to-service crossing, including authority, protocol, consistency, failure, migration, and rollout consequences.
evals.expected_output: The architecture method builds Crossing records and chooses the smallest topology whose contracts survive stated failures.
expectations: The agent selects go-system-architecture.
It materializes from, to, authority, protocol, interaction, consistency, failure, migration, consequence, and proof.

evals.prompt: The runtime topology and protocol are accepted. Decide which Go package and file own the client construction.
evals.expected_output: Code placement routes to go-implementation-ownership.
expectations: The agent selects go-implementation-ownership.
It does not reopen the accepted crossing.

evals.prompt: A proposal adds a second service and queue for one low-volume synchronous path without a distinct failure or scale force. Decide topology.
evals.expected_output: Reject the new boundary and keep the simpler existing component interaction.
expectations: The Crossing record names no force earned by the extra service and queue.
The agent prefers the smallest topology instead of speculative isolation.

evals.prompt: The component diagram exists, but authority, failure behavior, migration, and mixed-version rollout are blank for one new crossing. Is design complete?
evals.expected_output: No: implementation would still invent material boundary contracts.
expectations: The agent refuses completion from a topology picture.
It returns the undispositioned Crossing fields exactly.

evals.prompt: The proof obligation, oracle, and PostgreSQL proving layer are accepted. Implement the non-routine concurrent transaction test only.
evals.expected_output: The test method builds executable proof with deterministic controls, independent oracle, command, cleanup, and result.
expectations: The agent selects go-test-implementation.
It uses real PostgreSQL for engine semantics and does not reopen accepted behavior.

evals.prompt: The wrong behavior, oracle, and proving layer are disputed. Decide how the change should be falsified; do not write test code.
evals.expected_output: Open falsification design routes to go-test-strategy.
expectations: The agent selects go-test-strategy.
It stops before fixtures or executable test code.

evals.prompt: Implement an accepted shutdown-order test. The proposed harness sleeps longer than the timeout and polls a flag.
evals.expected_output: Use deterministic time and a blocking-state oracle rather than wall-clock sleep and polling.
expectations: The ExecutableProof names the wrong schedule and independent lifecycle observable.
It uses synctest or an existing fake clock at the smallest valid layer.

evals.prompt: The test file exists and go test exits 0, but the -run pattern matched zero tests and no test event was checked. Is test implementation complete?
evals.expected_output: No: executable proof did not execute.
expectations: The agent refuses completion from exit zero.
It requires evidence that the named test ran and observed the independent oracle.

evals.prompt: Test Design only. The wrong behavior, deterministic controls, oracle, and proving layer for a cross-service unknown outcome are non-obvious.
evals.expected_output: The strategy method builds ProofObligation records and stops before test code.
expectations: The agent selects go-test-strategy.
It names fail-before, controls, fixture, independent oracle, layer, command, cleanup, and reopen.

evals.prompt: A claim already has a command and result; decide only whether that existing evidence proves repository-wide readiness.
evals.expected_output: Existing claim boundaries route to go-verification-before-completion.
expectations: The agent selects go-verification-before-completion.
It does not redesign proof when the question is what current evidence establishes.

evals.prompt: A critical transaction invariant is proposed for an HTTP mock test because the feature matters. Choose the proving layer and oracle.
evals.expected_output: Use the smallest real-PostgreSQL layer that can observe atomic state; criticality alone does not justify an unrelated HTTP layer.
expectations: The ProofObligation names the regression the mock cannot see.
It chooses an independent database observable and deterministic controls.

evals.prompt: The test plan lists commands and broad coverage, but no fail-before discriminator or independent oracle for one material risk. Is Test Design complete?
evals.expected_output: No: one obligation has no falsifier and can false-pass.
expectations: The agent refuses completion from command breadth.
It returns the missing wrong behavior, oracle, and reopen condition.

evals.prompt: An in-progress rebase has conflicted generated and manual Go files. Resolve the active conflict, prove it, and continue the authorized operation.
evals.expected_output: The merge method reconstructs both intents per hunk, follows canonical authority, stages only resolved paths, and continues the active operation.
expectations: The agent selects merge-conflict-resolution after inspecting status and operation state.
It preserves unrelated work and regenerates from canonical source instead of choosing a whole side.

evals.prompt: No merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert, or unmerged path is active. Implement an accepted local Go change.
evals.expected_output: Ordinary implementation routes to go-coder.
expectations: The agent selects go-coder.
It does not manufacture conflict-resolution work from an ordinary dirty tree.

evals.prompt: One merge hunk chooses between a hand-edited generated file and a changed canonical OpenAPI source. Both sides compile. Resolve the intent.
evals.expected_output: Preserve the canonical OpenAPI intent, regenerate output, and reject the hand edit.
expectations: The agent states both hunk intents before resolving.
It uses source authority and matching drift proof rather than compile success.

evals.prompt: Conflict markers are gone, but one unmerged path remains, unrelated files are staged, and the affected test was not run. Is resolution complete?
evals.expected_output: No: operation state, staging scope, and proof remain invalid.
expectations: The agent refuses completion from marker removal.
It leaves unresolved authority intact or fixes exact staging and proof before continuing.

evals.prompt: The client-visible timeout response and replay semantics are accepted. Decide the internal per-hop deadlines, retry spend, and overload disposition that can satisfy them.
evals.expected_output: Reliability owns budget arithmetic after the observable API clause is closed.
expectations: The agent selects go-reliability for failure-handling policy.
It preserves the accepted client contract without reopening status or replay meaning.

evals.prompt: The operator signal is accepted, but the open defect is that its http.route label is captured before chi routing and sometimes falls back to the raw URL path.
evals.expected_output: Chi owns route identity source and middleware position; observability policy stays fixed.
expectations: The agent selects go-chi.
It proves route-template extraction after routing and never substitutes raw path.

evals.prompt: Implementation is authorized, but accepted behavior does not decide whether percent-w may expose a dependency sentinel through the package boundary. Choose the first owner.
evals.expected_output: Go idiomatic closes caller-visible error identity before go-coder implements it.
expectations: The agent selects go-idiomatic for semantic ownership.
It does not let implementation invent the exported error contract.

evals.prompt: A production test regressed and the cause and owner are unknown. The ticket says fix the handler. Choose the method before editing.
evals.expected_output: Unknown cause routes to first-broken-invariant debugging before implementation.
expectations: The agent selects go-systematic-debugging and establishes the signal.
It does not assume the symptom location is the causal owner.

evals.prompt: An accepted implementation is interrupted by an active cherry-pick conflict in the same files. Decide the immediate owner.
evals.expected_output: Active operation state routes to merge-conflict-resolution before ordinary implementation continues.
expectations: The agent selects merge-conflict-resolution.
It reconstructs both hunk intents and preserves the accepted implementation outcome.

evals.prompt: The local goroutine lifecycle is correct, but a committed effect can be redelivered after process loss and acknowledgment loss. Choose the owner.
evals.expected_output: Durable recovery routes to go-distributed, not local happens-before.
expectations: The agent selects go-distributed.
It materializes duplicate, unknown, redrive, and reconciliation outcomes across process loss.

evals.prompt: A shutdown deadline is accepted, but a sender can remain blocked forever because the receiver returns early and no join edge exists. Choose the owner.
evals.expected_output: Concurrency owns unblock and join correctness; another timeout would only mask the leak.
expectations: The agent selects go-concurrency.
It names the blocking send, receiver exit, unblock mechanism, and join.

evals.prompt: A cache query is correct, but the open decision is whether the cache or PostgreSQL is authoritative and how stale values repair. Choose the owner.
evals.expected_output: Authority and derived-surface lifecycle route to go-data-architecture.
expectations: The agent selects go-data-architecture.
It closes writer, lag, repair, and retention before runtime cache access policy.

evals.prompt: The storage owner is known, but business has not decided whether a duplicate command is a no-op, conflict, or repeated acceptance. Choose the owner.
evals.expected_output: Duplicate meaning is a domain invariant before data representation.
expectations: The agent selects go-domain-invariant.
It defines accepted sameness, effect order, and rejection before choosing constraints.

evals.prompt: A local transaction can report commit outcome unknown, and another service must reconcile whether the external effect applied. Choose the primary owner for recovery.
evals.expected_output: Cross-owner unknown outcome and reconciliation route to go-distributed after the local transaction classifies its result.
expectations: The agent selects go-distributed for the end-to-end recovery decision.
It preserves the local commit classification and defines applied, unapplied, and unknown reconciliation.

evals.prompt: The canary metric is already defined. Decide whether its threshold, observation window, rollback trigger, and release gate make the candidate shippable.
evals.expected_output: Delivery owns rollout acceptance using the existing operator signal.
expectations: The agent selects go-delivery-platform.
It records the signal as gate proof without redesigning telemetry.

evals.prompt: gRPC registration and status mapping are accepted, but a caller can spoof tenant metadata and reach another tenant's asset. Choose the owner.
evals.expected_output: Security owns verified principal, authorization enforcement, asset reachability, and denial proof.
expectations: The agent selects go-security.
It treats metadata as untrusted until verifier-owned identity and negative proof close the path.

evals.prompt: A shorter refactor changes nil versus empty and exported error identity. Names and control flow are otherwise clearer. Choose the owner.
evals.expected_output: Caller-visible Go semantics route to go-idiomatic before readability judgment.
expectations: The agent selects go-idiomatic.
It materializes caller observations and rejects behavior-changing simplification.

evals.prompt: Retry and overload behavior are accepted. The open decision is which SLI and alert tell operators the degradation is harming users without paging on every cause.
evals.expected_output: Observability owns the operator question, symptom signal, labels, readers, privacy, and alert.
expectations: The agent selects go-observability.
It alerts on the user-visible symptom and keeps causes as correlated diagnostic signals.

evals.prompt: Capacity measurements are accepted. Decide whether to shed, queue, degrade, or retry when arrivals exceed that capacity.
evals.expected_output: Reliability owns overload and failure disposition after performance establishes the ceiling.
expectations: The agent selects go-reliability.
It uses the measured ceiling as input and defines bounded work and visible terminal behavior.

evals.prompt: The open decision is whether two components should communicate by a new runtime crossing. Package placement can wait. Choose the owner.
evals.expected_output: System architecture closes the crossing, protocol, authority, failure, and migration before Go placement.
expectations: The agent selects go-system-architecture.
It does not use package layout to decide runtime topology.

evals.prompt: The exact wrong behavior, independent oracle, deterministic controls, and proving layer are accepted. Only test code and fixture mechanics remain.
evals.expected_output: Test implementation owns executable proof; Test Design is not reopened.
expectations: The agent selects go-test-implementation.
It preserves the accepted ProofObligation and builds the smallest runnable falsifier.

evals.prompt: No proof exists yet and the open question is which falsifier, oracle, controls, and layer should prove the future behavior. Choose the owner.
evals.expected_output: Test strategy designs future proof; verification has no existing evidence to bound.
expectations: The agent selects go-test-strategy.
It stops with ProofObligation records rather than claiming verification.

evals.prompt: A retryable POST can commit before the client timeout. Select only the reference that changes key scope, reservation, replay, TTL, mismatch, and unknown-outcome judgment.
evals.expected_output: Load idempotency-and-replay.md and no unrelated API leaf unless another pressure independently appears.
expectations: The agent loads the idempotency leaf after stating its expected decision effect.
It does not load compatibility, error-profile, or async leaves without independent pressure.

evals.prompt: A metric label sometimes uses the raw request path because route identity is empty. Select the one chi leaf that changes label-source judgment.
evals.expected_output: Load route-labels.md and apply post-routing bounded identity without loading unrelated fallback or middleware leaves.
expectations: The agent loads route-labels.md.
It treats empty route template as unmatched and never falls back to raw path.

evals.prompt: An accepted OpenAPI change tempts a direct edit to generated Go. Select the one implementation leaf that changes source and proof ownership.
evals.expected_output: Load generated-source-of-truth-and-drift.md and edit the canonical source before generation and drift proof.
expectations: The agent loads the generated-source leaf.
It does not load collection or modernization leaves without another pressure.

evals.prompt: A fan-out limits active workers but allows unlimited queued submissions. Select only the leaf that changes the concurrency-bound judgment.
evals.expected_output: Load bounded-work-and-backpressure.md and count queued work plus the submission path.
expectations: The agent loads the bounded-work leaf.
It does not load timer or shared-state leaves without an independent defect.

evals.prompt: A populated table needs a backfill and concurrent index, but this repository's migrator wraps migrations in one transaction. Select the decision-changing leaf.
evals.expected_output: Load migrations-in-one-transaction.md and split additive DDL from application-owned backfill.
expectations: The agent loads the migration leaf.
It does not load derived-surface policy when publication or retention is unchanged.

evals.prompt: A release carries a schema migration while old and new binaries overlap. Select only the delivery leaf that changes the rollout gate.
evals.expected_output: Load migration-rollout-window.md and disposition mixed-version safety and rollback.
expectations: The agent loads the migration rollout leaf.
It does not load publication trust or required-check leaves without independent pressure.

evals.prompt: Terminal states and forbidden reopen paths decide whether a command is legal. Select the one domain decision leaf that changes the invariant.
evals.expected_output: Load state-machine-and-transition-rules.md and define forbidden movement and terminal policy.
expectations: The agent loads the state-transition leaf.
It does not load replay or generic violation leaves without another pressure.

evals.prompt: A .proto compatibility claim rests on green generation and breaking gates. Select the one gRPC leaf that bounds those gates.
evals.expected_output: Load proto-contract-gates.md and hand-classify what the gates did and did not compare.
expectations: The agent loads the proto gate leaf.
It does not load status mapping without a changed failure path.

evals.prompt: An exported adapter wraps a dependency sentinel and callers may branch with errors.Is. Select the one semantic leaf that changes the decision.
evals.expected_output: Load error-contracts.md and decide intentional error identity rather than trusting lint.
expectations: The agent loads the error contract leaf.
It does not load aliasing, lifetime, or nil leaves without independent pressure.

evals.prompt: A deduplication merges response and cleanup branches that may preserve different status and error identities. Select the one simplification leaf that changes judgment.
evals.expected_output: Load behavior-preserving-boundary.md and enumerate observable classes before merging.
expectations: The agent loads the behavior-boundary leaf.
It does not load indirection economics unless a helper boundary independently changes.

evals.prompt: A metric adds a tenant-controlled label and changes its unit. Select the one observability leaf that changes identity and cardinality judgment.
evals.expected_output: Load metric-identity-and-cardinality.md and size the exported label product and unit.
expectations: The agent loads the metric leaf.
It does not load logs, trace correlation, or readiness leaves without another signal pressure.

evals.prompt: A candidate adds sync.Pool after allocs/op fell, but reuse safety and latency attribution are unclear. Select the performance review leaf that changes judgment.
evals.expected_output: Load allocation-and-pooling.md and require bottleneck attribution plus miss and reuse safety.
expectations: The agent loads the allocation leaf.
It does not load scaling or evidence recapture leaves without independent pressure.

evals.prompt: An outbound wait is added to a request path under the repository's 8 second parent budget. Select the one reliability leaf that changes timeout judgment.
evals.expected_output: Load request-budget.md and derive a sub-budget from the existing relation.
expectations: The agent loads the request-budget leaf.
It does not load admission or shutdown leaves without independent pressure.

evals.prompt: A tenant-supplied URL can become an outbound webhook destination. Select the one security leaf that changes SSRF and destination judgment.
evals.expected_output: Load outbound-egress.md and reuse pinned authority plus the post-DNS gate.
expectations: The agent loads the outbound egress leaf.
It does not load unrelated identity, disclosure, or abuse leaves without independent pressure.

evals.prompt: A new strictly internal synchronous service call needs protocol and exposure decisions. Select the one architecture leaf that changes the crossing.
evals.expected_output: Load inter-service-protocol-selection.md and classify consumers, protocol, exposure, and correlation per neighbor.
expectations: The agent loads the protocol-selection leaf.
It does not load unrelated current-boundary leaves without another pressure.

evals.prompt: A Go test fails only under CI repetition and shuffle. Select the one debugging leaf that changes the next experiment.
evals.expected_output: Load flaky-repro-controls-go.md and move one recorded control at a time.
expectations: The agent loads the flaky-control leaf.
It does not load runtime forensics for a local repeatable test.

evals.prompt: An accepted proof obligation depends on PostgreSQL row locks and concurrent claims. Select the one test leaf that changes the harness.
evals.expected_output: Load postgres-integration-proof.md and use the real pgtest database-per-test fixture.
expectations: The agent loads the PostgreSQL proof leaf.
It does not load deterministic time or generic proving-layer leaves without another pressure.

evals.prompt: A proof target crosses a durable boundary and a mock call can false-pass. Select the one strategy leaf that changes the oracle.
evals.expected_output: Load boundary-observables.md and choose a durable independent observable.
expectations: The agent loads the boundary-observable leaf.
It does not load validation-command or generic obligation leaves without independent pressure.

evals.prompt: The claim depends on generated SQLC output and a migration. Select the one verification leaf that separates drift from behavior and rehearsal.
evals.expected_output: Load generated-api-and-migration-verification.md and bound each proof surface separately.
expectations: The agent loads the generated and migration verification leaf.
It does not also load generic claim mapping without an independent ambiguity.

evals.prompt: Review internal/instructioneval/hardmutations/BlockedSender. Find the exact lifecycle defect, consequence, smallest owner, and one proof that fails on the fixture.
evals.expected_output: A caller that stops receiving can strand the sender forever; fix cancellation or ownership at the shared send loop and prove early abandonment joins it.
expectations: The agent points to the unguarded output send and missing stop/join rather than adding a timeout to the caller.
It proposes a deterministic early-return proof that observes sender termination.

evals.prompt: Review internal/instructioneval/hardmutations/DefaultPageSize. PublishedDefaultPageSize is the deployed contract and the schema differ is green. Find the exact compatibility defect and proof.
evals.expected_output: The implicit default changes from 20 to 50, a client-visible compatibility break that schema drift can miss.
expectations: The agent materializes old and new default cells and their client consequence.
It proposes a consumer-visible omitted-parameter proof and migration disposition.

evals.prompt: Review internal/instructioneval/hardmutations/TestMiddlewareOrder. Find why the test can pass with the wrong middleware order and name the smallest replacement oracle.
evals.expected_output: Status is order-insensitive; use a before/after sequence recorder and route-tree proof.
expectations: The agent identifies the false-pass in the concrete status-only assertion.
It proposes a recorder whose expected sequence reverses when middleware order is wrong.

evals.prompt: Review internal/instructioneval/hardmutations/ParallelHandlers against an accepted replacement of the legacy handler. Find the exact defect, smallest owner, and proof.
evals.expected_output: The legacy root fallback remains an alternate serving path; remove it at route composition and prove no request reaches it.
expectations: The agent traces the far-side fallback instead of accepting the new /items handler test.
It removes the superseded path and proposes topology plus unmatched-route proof.

evals.prompt: Review internal/instructioneval/hardmutations/MetricLabel. Find the operator, privacy, and cardinality defect and the smallest repository-owned replacement.
evals.expected_output: Raw caller-controlled URL paths create unbounded labels and disclosure; use the bounded route template after routing or no route label.
expectations: The agent identifies the concrete raw-path sink and its label product.
It proposes proof with high-cardinality inputs and unmatched routes without raw-path fallback.

evals.prompt: Review internal/instructioneval/hardmutations/RetryBudget under an accepted 8 second end-to-end request budget. Find the exact budget defect and proof.
evals.expected_output: Three 3 second background attempts plus sleeps can exceed the parent budget; propagate the parent and clamp attempts to remaining time.
expectations: The agent performs worst-case spend arithmetic and notices context.Background drops the parent.
It proposes deterministic elapsed-budget proof, including sleeps and terminal response room.

evals.prompt: A flaky readiness test calls internal/instructioneval/hardmutations/SleepUntilReady as its fix. Diagnose the defect and choose the smallest red-capable proof.
evals.expected_output: A fixed sleep masks the missing condition and remains scheduler-dependent; reproduce and wait on the real readiness edge deterministically.
expectations: The agent rejects time.Sleep as a causal repair.
It establishes failure frequency and replaces time with a condition or synctest observable.

evals.prompt: Review internal/instructioneval/hardmutations/CachedUser. Find the exact access-policy defects and decide whether the cache should exist.
evals.expected_output: The cache has no measured need, tenant-safe key contract, freshness bound, invalidation owner, or bounded fallback; remove it until those exist.
expectations: The agent applies YAGNI and rejects the global sync.Map rather than wrapping it in more abstraction.
It names the missing invalidation and stale-read proof if a measured need later reopens the cache.

evals.prompt: Review internal/instructioneval/hardmutations/WrappedDependencySentinel as an exported adapter result. Find the exact caller-visible semantic defect and proof.
evals.expected_output: Percent-w publishes dependency error identity; translate to a package-owned sentinel or keep the cause opaque according to the accepted caller contract.
expectations: The agent traces errors.Is visibility instead of praising wrapping mechanically.
It proposes positive package-owned identity proof and a negative opacity proof for the dependency sentinel.
